thinEvidence.note: Audience monetization is highly skewed; the vast majority of pages earn nothing.

thinEvidence.text: Most NFTs only point to an off-chain image that can be altered or lost, so the token confers no durable ownership of the artwork
thinEvidence.note: Most ERC-721 metadata referenced HTTP or IPFS URLs; link rot and swapped images were documented repeatedly.

thinEvidence.text: Most online advice on making money with AI comes from people who have not made money with AI
thinEvidence.note: An unverifiable characterization of other creators.

thinEvidence.text: Most people who try to sell their expertise as a course find little paying demand
thinEvidence.note: Course marketplaces show a long tail where most courses sell few or no copies.

thinEvidence.text: Most prediction-market users lose money; winnings concentrate in a small number of sophisticated accounts
thinEvidence.note: On-chain analyses show a large majority of accounts are net losers with profits concentrated in a few hundred wallets, matching sportsbook and retail-trading patterns.

thinEvidence.text: Most seller leads convert only after many follow-up contacts, so a CRM and persistent follow-up are essential.
thinEvidence.note: Multi-touch conversion is a general sales finding; the specific count is folklore.

thinEvidence.text: Most side-hustle income goes to living expenses or discretionary spending rather than building wealth
thinEvidence.note: Bankrate finds only a minority save any of it; consistent with other surveys.

thinEvidence.text: Most AI side hustles promoted online never earn their operator a dollar.
thinEvidence.note: Consistent with survey data on side-hustle earnings, though stated without evidence by a promoter of the remaining five.

thinEvidence.text: Motivational hustle content lifts mood but is not practical advice
thinEvidence.note: Framing about how to interpret a genre of content.

thinEvidence.text: Multiple faceless channels can generate five figures a month
thinEvidence.note: Most faceless channels never reach monetization, and five-figure monthly claims come from operators selling courses.

thinEvidence.text: A new channel's first videos get almost no views until the algorithm learns who to show them to
thinEvidence.note: Recommendation systems need watch data before surfacing a new channel.

thinEvidence.text: New competing short-term rental supply can turn a profitable unit cash-flow negative
thinEvidence.note: Revenue per listing fell in many US markets as supply grew after 2022.

thinEvidence.text: NFT project communities police doubt as FUD, so scrutiny of a project's viability is suppressed
thinEvidence.note: A description of community norms and framing rather than a measurable outcome.

thinEvidence.text: NFT resale royalties are enforced by marketplaces rather than the token, so they are easily bypassed
thinEvidence.note: Major marketplaces made creator royalties optional in 2022-2023 and royalty income collapsed, confirming they were never on-chain enforced.

thinEvidence.text: Niche does not matter for short-form content because the creator's personality is the differentiator
thinEvidence.note: A framing about creative strategy with no clear evidence either way.

thinEvidence.text: Nobody has lost money holding an S&P 500 index fund for twenty years or more
thinEvidence.note: True for every rolling twenty-year period in nominal terms since 1926, though real returns were near zero in a few.

thinEvidence.text: Number of users is the best measure of whether a startup has created wealth.
thinEvidence.note: Usage is a strong signal but can be bought or unmonetizable; revenue and retention matter too.

thinEvidence.text: Once the skills are mastered, online money falls out of thin air
thinEvidence.note: Even the source's own test needed daily filming for a week and yielded modest profit.

thinEvidence.text: One arbitraged short-term rental unit nets a couple of thousand dollars a month once set up
thinEvidence.note: Market data show falling revenue per listing and many arbitraged units earning below rent and costs, so a couple of thousand net is not typical.

thinEvidence.text: A one percent annual fee compounds into a large share of a portfolio over decades
thinEvidence.note: Fee drag compounds; standard calculators show one percent costing roughly a quarter of terminal wealth over thirty-plus years.

thinEvidence.text: Online marketplace sales peak in the fourth-quarter holiday season
thinEvidence.note: US retail and e-commerce sales follow a well-documented seasonal peak from October through December.

thinEvidence.text: Only knowledge that cannot be taught in a classroom earns outsized pay; trainable skills get commoditized to the cost of training
thinEvidence.note: Scarce, hard-to-codify skills do earn a premium, but many trainable credentialed professions still pay very well because entry is restricted.

thinEvidence.text: Only a small minority of course buyers ever complete the course
thinEvidence.note: Online course completion rates are commonly reported in the 5 to 15 percent range, though paid cohorts do better.

thinEvidence.text: Only a small minority of third-party Amazon sellers earn even a modest income
thinEvidence.note: Seller surveys show many sellers make little, but the share depends on how dormant and part-time accounts are counted.

thinEvidence.text: Options spreads let small accounts take positions that would otherwise require far more capital
thinEvidence.note: Defined-risk spreads do reduce capital requirements; that is their mechanical purpose.

thinEvidence.text: An ordinary earner who saves a large majority of take-home pay can reach financial independence in about a decade
thinEvidence.note: The savings-rate math holds under reasonable return assumptions; the claim is conditional on actually saving a large majority, which is the hard part but not a false promise.

thinEvidence.text: Ordinary people have little chance of out-gaming banks and credit-card companies at their own products
thinEvidence.note: Card issuers design rewards and promotional offers around revolver behaviour; their profitability depends on most customers not winning the game.

thinEvidence.text: Outrageous pitches filter the audience down to the most impressionable buyers, like scam emails with typos
thinEvidence.note: The typo-filter hypothesis for scam email has research support; the extension to gurus is inference.

thinEvidence.text: Overseas-to-doorstep dropshipping depended on a duty exemption for small packages and subsidized shipping that no longer exist
thinEvidence.note: De minimis was suspended in 2025 and subsidized postal rates ended; landed costs rose sharply.

thinEvidence.text: Paid ads only amplify products that already sell; they cannot fix a weak product
thinEvidence.note: Ad performance follows product appeal and creative; ads on unproven listings mainly burn budget.

thinEvidence.text: Paid coaching gives a better return than a college degree
thinEvidence.note: The college wage premium is large and well measured, while coaching returns rest on self-reported, selected testimonials.

thinEvidence.text: Paid-ad dropshipping is only profitable when revenue per ad dollar clears product cost, fees and shipping
thinEvidence.note: Return on ad spend must exceed the inverse of the margin after goods and fees; this is basic unit economics.

thinEvidence.text: Paid mentorship gives a guru visibility into students' winning products, which can be copied to compete against them
thinEvidence.note: A documented allegation in this case; prevalence across mentorships is unknown.

thinEvidence.text: Paid pick sellers force plays when losing to keep subscribers
thinEvidence.note: Plausible incentive but no systematic evidence on tipster behavior.

thinEvidence.text: Paid social ads are a learnable skill in days and a money machine for any product
thinEvidence.note: Ad platforms are easy to use but hard to profit from, and many small advertisers never reach a positive return.

thinEvidence.text: A partnership with a major asset manager makes a crypto token a good investment
thinEvidence.note: Partnerships rarely send value to a token's holders, and the news is usually priced in by the time it is announced.

thinEvidence.text: Paying down a mortgage early is a risk-free return equal to the mortgage rate
thinEvidence.note: Avoided interest is a guaranteed pre-tax return at the loan rate, less any lost interest deduction.

thinEvidence.text: Paying for high-ticket coaching returns many times its cost
thinEvidence.note: The returns cited are selected client testimonials; no independent data shows typical buyers recover high coaching fees.

thinEvidence.text: Paying prop-firm challenge fees is an investment because the first payouts recover the fees lost on blown accounts
thinEvidence.note: Most challenge buyers never get funded or paid, so for the typical buyer the fees are a sunk loss, not tuition that pays back.

thinEvidence.text: Paying for recruits' event tickets is used to create guilt and reinforce company doctrine
thinEvidence.note: Consistent with ex-member accounts and high-control-group literature but not systematically measured.

thinEvidence.text: Peer-to-peer lending reliably gives retail lenders a positive return
thinEvidence.note: Diversified lenders on major platforms mostly earned positive returns, but defaults and platform failures left many retail lenders with losses.

thinEvidence.text: People fail to get rich because they never do the math on what it takes, not because it is hard
thinEvidence.note: This is a motivational framing; goal arithmetic is trivial and the difficulty lies in customer acquisition and retention, which the framing waves away.

thinEvidence.text: People who need money are the worst MLM recruits; those who do not need it succeed
thinEvidence.note: Recruits with existing networks and capital do outperform, but the claim mostly describes who survives the attrition rather than a mechanism that helps recruits.

thinEvidence.text: Personalised low-cost jewelry sells at many times unit cost because of high perceived value
thinEvidence.note: Markups on personalised jewelry are wide, but customer acquisition cost absorbs most of the spread.

thinEvidence.text: Personalized cold pitches and repeated follow-ups are how new freelancers land their first clients
thinEvidence.note: Personalized outreach and follow-up raise reply rates, but response rates stay low and many first deals come from referrals and platforms.

thinEvidence.text: Pinterest works as a free search-driven traffic source for print-on-demand stores
thinEvidence.note: Pinterest can send search traffic to product pins, but results for new accounts are slow and uncertain.

thinEvidence.text: Ad-platform attribution misses some purchases, so dashboard numbers understate true results
thinEvidence.note: Post-privacy-change attribution loss on Meta is well documented; advertisers routinely reconcile against store orders.

thinEvidence.text: Platforms push ordinary users into creator programs because free content benefits the platform.
thinEvidence.note: Platforms do onboard new accounts into creator and bonus programs; the incentive is clear even if the motive is inferred.

thinEvidence.text: Play-to-earn scholarship schemes let account owners take a large cut of players' earnings, leaving players at or below local minimum wage
thinEvidence.note: Reporting and economy analyses documented sub-minimum-wage earnings after the 2021 downturn, though earlier earnings had briefly exceeded local wages.

thinEvidence.text: Player prop markets are priced less sharply than main markets and offer more exploitable edges
thinEvidence.note: Props and other low-volume markets are widely documented as less efficient than main lines, though books offset this with low limits and quick restrictions.

thinEvidence.text: Prediction-market odds forecast about as well as professional forecasters on economic questions but have notable big misses
thinEvidence.note: Studies find calibration comparable to experts on liquid macro markets, with thin markets and low-volume events showing large errors.

thinEvidence.text: Prediction markets raise no capital for productive use; they only transfer money from retail bettors to platforms, quants and insiders
thinEvidence.note: They do not fund businesses, but their forecasts are an information good used by media and hedgers, so pure transfer is not the whole picture.

thinEvidence.text: Pricing offers off recently sold comparable properties avoids needing to estimate repair costs
thinEvidence.note: Comps help, but investors price on repair cost, so ignoring it leads to offers buyers reject.

thinEvidence.text: Print-on-demand margins are thin because the printer's base cost takes most of the sale price
thinEvidence.note: Base costs on major print-on-demand platforms leave a few dollars per item before fees, ads and refunds.

thinEvidence.text: Print-on-demand t-shirts on Amazon earn passive income if you find small untapped niches
thinEvidence.note: Tier limits, saturation and takedowns keep typical print-on-demand royalties small, and untapped niches close fast once found.

thinEvidence.text: Private-label-rights templates let sellers list new digital products quickly without creating them from scratch
thinEvidence.note: PLR templates do cut creation time, though the same templates go to many sellers, so the listings are hard to tell apart.

thinEvidence.text: Private-labeling a validated product under your own brand raises margins and cuts returns
thinEvidence.note: Brand owners do report higher margins; the example is one seller's anecdote.

thinEvidence.text: A product branded for a specific niche community can still succeed on Amazon
thinEvidence.note: Niche branding is a real differentiator and 'can' is modest, but most new Amazon private-label products fail to reach profitability and niche wins attract copycats.

thinEvidence.text: A product's markup over its unit cost is a return comparable to or better than stock-market returns
thinEvidence.note: Markup ignores overhead, marketing and capital at risk; it is not an annual return on invested capital and cannot be compared to market returns.

thinEvidence.text: Professional traders use options to cut capital and risk per trade
thinEvidence.note: Professionals do use options for capital efficiency and defined risk, but usually hedged and with risk controls retail traders lack.

thinEvidence.text: Profitable sports betting comes from exploiting pricing discrepancies between sportsbooks, not sports knowledge
thinEvidence.note: Documented long-run edges are mostly price-based such as line shopping and beating the closing line, though some sharp bettors win with their own models.

thinEvidence.text: Proof-of-work mining rewards whoever can buy the most hardware and electricity, so returns concentrate with existing capital
thinEvidence.note: Mining economics scale with capital and cheap power; hash rate is dominated by large industrial operations and pools.

thinEvidence.text: A property earns roughly double as a short-term rental what it earns as a long-term rental
thinEvidence.note: Gross short-term revenue can beat rent in strong markets, but net of fees, cleaning, vacancy and management the premium is far smaller and often negative.

thinEvidence.text: Proprietary buy/sell indicators reliably flag over- and undervalued zones to trade
thinEvidence.note: Oscillator-style indicators are lagging transforms of price; no independent evidence shows paid indicator suites produce an edge after costs.

thinEvidence.text: Public stock investing is a scam because the investor cannot control the outcome
thinEvidence.note: Diversified index investing has delivered positive real returns over every long period on record; lack of control is not fraud.

thinEvidence.text: Publishing a book or course makes you an authority that prospects say yes to before hearing the offer
thinEvidence.note: Authority signals help conversion modestly, but most self-published books and courses reach few readers and do not presell prospects.

thinEvidence.text: Publishing books for a different holiday each season keeps print-on-demand income steady through the year
thinEvidence.note: Stacking seasonal titles smooths income somewhat, but each holiday spike is short and competitive and the fourth quarter still dominates.

thinEvidence.text: Raising prices attracts buyers who will pay almost any price to solve their problem, so most sellers should charge premium prices
thinEvidence.note: Some sellers underprice, but demand is price-sensitive for most offers; anecdotes of raised prices selling more are selected cases.

thinEvidence.text: Real-estate crowdfunding lets an ordinary investor raise other people's money to buy property with none of their own
thinEvidence.note: Raising a fund means securities-law filings, offering costs and a track record investors trust; first-timers rarely raise money this way.

thinEvidence.text: Real estate is forgiving enough that even a mistaken purchase still makes money
thinEvidence.note: Leveraged property bought badly can and often does lose money, as foreclosure waves show; early wins in rising markets do not generalize.

thinEvidence.text: Recreating already-trending designs with AI is the easiest way to get print-on-demand sales
thinEvidence.note: Following proven demand helps, but copied trend designs face heavy competition and risk copyright and trademark takedowns.

thinEvidence.text: A recurring passive income stream is financially equivalent to a lump sum invested at a fixed yield
thinEvidence.note: The arithmetic holds but the equivalence ignores that business cash flow is riskier, less durable and less transferable than invested capital.

thinEvidence.text: Regulators are not enforcing existing authority to block event contracts on war, terrorism and assassination
thinEvidence.note: Such contracts are live on major platforms despite statutory authority to prohibit them; the regulator has instead sued states that tried to intervene.

thinEvidence.text: Reinvesting early side-hustle profits into tools, marketing and outsourcing is what lifts a side hustle into the top tier
thinEvidence.note: Reinvesting is needed to grow, but it cannot fix a business with no demand, and crediting top earners' success to it is survivorship bias.

thinEvidence.text: A rental property that does not cash-flow from day one should not be bought; promises it will pay later are a trap
thinEvidence.note: Negative-cash-flow 'value-add' deals do fail often, but renovation plays can work when underwritten carefully; the rule is conservative rather than universal.

thinEvidence.text: Reposting old viral videos keeps sales going with no new work
thinEvidence.note: Platforms de-rank duplicate content and product interest fades, so reposting does not keep sales going without new work.

thinEvidence.text: Retail bettors on prediction markets face quantitative market-making firms, a structural disadvantage research cannot close
thinEvidence.note: Professional market makers do capture spread from retail flow, but retail traders with genuine information edges can still win; no data isolates retail returns on these platforms.

thinEvidence.text: Retail and online arbitrage needs the least capital but cannot scale into a business because supply is capped by store purchase limits
thinEvidence.note: Clearance deals are one-off and retailers cap quantities, so arbitrage income is irregular and labour-intensive; this is widely acknowledged even by its promoters.

thinEvidence.text: Retail traders hold losing option positions open after announcements even though volatility has subsided
thinEvidence.note: The study documents a disposition-effect pattern consistent with the broader retail-investor behaviour literature.

thinEvidence.text: Retirement accounts can be tapped before the standard age without penalty through substantially equal periodic payments
thinEvidence.note: US tax code section 72(t) allows penalty-free SEPP withdrawals; Roth conversion ladders are another route.

thinEvidence.text: Reusing other people's video ads risks account bans and competes with identical creatives
thinEvidence.note: Copyright and ad-policy enforcement is real, and duplicate creatives fatigue faster.

thinEvidence.text: Review swapping among course members to seed book reviews violates platform rules and risks account bans
thinEvidence.note: Major retailers prohibit reciprocal and incentivized reviews and have removed reviews and banned accounts for it.

thinEvidence.text: Rewriting resumes with AI can be sold as a service for hundreds of dollars each
thinEvidence.note: Paid resume writing is a real market, but it is crowded and commoditized and beginners selling AI rewrites rarely command the top-end prices.

thinEvidence.text: A rising US manufacturing index signals an upcoming altcoin season
thinEvidence.note: The link rests on a couple of past cycles; with so few data points it has no demonstrated predictive power for altcoin prices.

thinEvidence.text: Rising shipping, goods and advertising costs are squeezing Amazon seller margins
thinEvidence.note: Vendor survey of self-selected sellers; consistent with Amazon fee increases and ad-cost inflation.

thinEvidence.text: Rotating debt through 0% balance-transfer offers is a gimmick that delays rather than solves overspending
thinEvidence.note: Transfers carry fees and promotional rates expire; research on balance-transfer users shows many end up with the same or larger balances.

thinEvidence.text: Running a paid online community or membership gives an ordinary creator recurring monthly income
thinEvidence.note: A few large communities earn well, but most paid communities have few members and high churn; the earnings shown are platform outliers.

thinEvidence.text: A running short-term rental needs only about an hour a week of the operator's time
thinEvidence.note: Guest messaging, turnover coordination, maintenance and reviews take far more unless a paid manager is hired, which cuts profit.

thinEvidence.text: Sales calls that amplify a prospect's pain and imagined future reliably close high-ticket coaching sales
thinEvidence.note: Problem-focused emotional selling does raise conversion, but closes still depend on qualified demand, and high-pressure tactics draw regulator scrutiny.

thinEvidence.text: Sales tax or VAT charged on Amazon's fees is a hidden cost that the fee calculator understates for unregistered sellers
thinEvidence.note: In the UK and EU, Amazon adds VAT to seller fees for non-VAT-registered sellers who cannot reclaim it, which reduces the net margin shown.

thinEvidence.text: Scaling matched betting through other people's bookmaker accounts breaks terms and risks confiscated balances
thinEvidence.note: Bookmaker terms bar betting on accounts not your own, and operators void bets and withhold balances when they detect it.

thinEvidence.text: Scaling one small product win across many products turns into thousands per month
thinEvidence.note: Most products fail to sell and each needs its own promotion, so one small win does not multiply into thousands a month.

thinEvidence.text: Schools teach nothing about money and teachers are poor, so formal education is the wrong place to learn wealth
thinEvidence.note: Personal-finance education is thin in most curricula, but educational attainment remains one of the strongest predictors of lifetime income and wealth.

thinEvidence.text: Scraped directory websites can earn passive ad or lead income for near-zero cost; it is a numbers game across many sites
thinEvidence.note: Search engines demote thin scraped and aggregator sites, so most such directories earn nothing and are not passive.

thinEvidence.text: AI script writing removes the main barrier that stops beginners from starting a YouTube channel
thinEvidence.note: Discoverability and retention, not scripts, are the binding constraints, and AI lowers the scripting barrier for every competitor equally.

thinEvidence.text: Seeing other traders' wins makes people take more risk and trade more
thinEvidence.note: An experimental study found this effect and social-trading platform data point the same way, though effect sizes vary.

thinEvidence.text: The self-employed must set aside a large share of income for taxes and buy their own health insurance
thinEvidence.note: Self-employment tax covers both halves of payroll tax and no employer subsidizes insurance.

thinEvidence.text: The self-employed pay the highest taxes of all
thinEvidence.note: Self-employment tax adds both halves of payroll tax, but deductions offset it; it is not clearly the highest.

thinEvidence.text: Self-employment is isolating and demands self-directed time management
thinEvidence.note: Surveys of the self-employed consistently report isolation and self-discipline as top challenges.

thinEvidence.text: Self-employment needs a multi-year savings runway before it covers living costs
thinEvidence.note: Runway advice is sensible; the right length varies by business.

thinEvidence.text: A self-publishing business scales to six figures by publishing more and better books
thinEvidence.note: Self-published book income is extremely skewed and most titles sell few copies, so volume alone does not reliably reach six figures.

thinEvidence.text: A self-reported bet tracker showing a high win rate proves a betting strategy works
thinEvidence.note: Unaudited trackers can omit bets, and a few months of results are dominated by variance.

thinEvidence.text: Sellers must buy premium offers themselves to be able to sell premium offers
thinEvidence.note: A motivational framing that also serves to sell the speaker's own premium coaching.

thinEvidence.text: Selling outcome-based retainers instead of hourly time is how service income scales
thinEvidence.note: Retainers do stabilize income, but outcome pricing shifts risk to the seller and needs a track record.

thinEvidence.text: Selling qualified leads to businesses is the easiest AI service to sell because the value is immediately measurable
thinEvidence.note: Lead generation has clear measurable value, but it is crowded and disputes over lead quality are common, so easiest is overstated.

thinEvidence.text: Selling same-day iron condors collects premium with a defined maximum loss
thinEvidence.note: Mechanically correct; the maximum loss exceeds the premium and occurs on large moves.

thinEvidence.text: Selling skill takes years of practice, not a five-day seminar
thinEvidence.note: Sales performance develops over years of practice; no short course has demonstrated otherwise.

thinEvidence.text: Selling stocks because they look expensive bets against momentum
thinEvidence.note: Momentum is one of the most robust return anomalies and valuation signals fire while prices are still rising.

thinEvidence.text: Service-based side hustles tie income to hours worked, so they do not scale into passive income.
thinEvidence.note: Definitional for services; income stops when delivery stops unless a team is hired.

thinEvidence.text: Setting a profit target larger than the stop-loss gives a trader an edge by itself
thinEvidence.note: Wider targets are hit less often, so the risk-reward ratio alone does not change expected value; an edge needs entries with predictive power.

thinEvidence.text: Setting a very short deadline makes work get done faster because work expands to fill the time available
thinEvidence.note: Deadlines do curb procrastination, but planning-fallacy research shows tight deadlines are routinely missed and can cut quality.

thinEvidence.text: Shipping from a domestic warehouse cuts delivery to days and improves reviews at the cost of margin
thinEvidence.note: Domestic fulfillment delivers in days; the trade-off is higher unit cost.

thinEvidence.text: Short-dated, just-out-of-the-money options are the best day-trading instrument because they are cheap and react most to price moves
thinEvidence.note: Retail option losses are concentrated in short-dated out-of-the-money contracts, where time decay and spreads eat the leverage.

thinEvidence.text: Short organic dropshipping tests typically yield hundreds, not thousands, in profit
thinEvidence.note: Published first-hand tests typically report modest profits, but the sample is self-selected.

thinEvidence.text: Short-term rental arbitrage scales linearly by adding units
thinEvidence.note: Each unit needs fresh capital, a willing landlord and more management, and regulation caps many markets, so linear scaling is a best case.

thinEvidence.text: Side hustling rises when the job market weakens and prices rise
thinEvidence.note: Plausible and consistent with the survey trend, but it is an analyst's interpretation rather than a tested relationship.

thinEvidence.text: Sizing up only after a daily profit cushion and adding to winners makes day-trading results consistent
thinEvidence.note: Position sizing can reshape the daily P&L pattern but cannot create an edge; the consistency evidence is one trader's own record.

thinEvidence.text: Small businesses will pay thousands of dollars a month for custom AI chatbots and workflow automations
thinEvidence.note: Off-the-shelf chatbot and automation tools cost tens to hundreds a month, so few small businesses pay agency retainers in the thousands for them.

thinEvidence.text: Small RV or mobile-home parks bought with seller financing are many times more profitable than single-family rentals
thinEvidence.note: Park yields run somewhat higher than single-family rentals for more work and risk, not many times higher, and low-cash seller financing is rare.

thinEvidence.text: A solo owner does every job, and constant task-switching is a mental cost
thinEvidence.note: Task-switching costs are documented in cognitive research; the business effect is anecdotal.

thinEvidence.text: Specific problem-solving titles get far more clicks than generic ones
thinEvidence.note: Click-through differences for specific versus generic titles are widely reported by creators.

thinEvidence.text: Sportsbooks push expert picks and analysis because they distract bettors from pricing, the only real edge
thinEvidence.note: A plausible incentive, but the motive is inferred rather than demonstrated.

thinEvidence.text: Spotting under-the-radar small-cap altcoins early lets retail buyers capture ten-fold or greater gains
thinEvidence.note: Most small-cap tokens lose most of their value or die; promoter-picked gems are a lottery where a few big winners hide many losers.

thinEvidence.text: Standard whole life policies pay agents most of the first-year base premium as commission, leaving little early cash value
thinEvidence.note: First-year whole life commissions commonly run from half to all of the base premium, and early cash values sit far below premiums paid.

thinEvidence.text: Starting to invest young matters most because time drives compounding
thinEvidence.note: Compounding scales with years invested.

thinEvidence.text: Starting a short-term rental business in a downturn means cheap furniture and less competition
thinEvidence.note: Supply exits can lower competition and furniture costs, but downturns also cut travel demand and nightly rates.

thinEvidence.text: A stay-at-home parent can earn meaningful income selling digital printables on Etsy working only during nap times
thinEvidence.note: Most Etsy shops earn very little, and digital printables are flooded with resold templates, so one seller's results don't carry over to most parents.

thinEvidence.text: Staying out of the range between pre-market and prior-day highs and lows avoids most losing day trades
thinEvidence.note: No independent test of this filter exists; the support is the seller's own picked backtest days.

thinEvidence.text: A stock trading above VWAP is intraday bullish and below VWAP bearish
thinEvidence.note: VWAP describes the day's average fill; it is widely watched but has little documented edge as a signal.

thinEvidence.text: Stocks reliably return about five percent a year above inflation over the long run
thinEvidence.note: Global equities have averaged about this real return over a century, but 'reliably' overstates it given multi-decade stretches of near-zero real returns.

thinEvidence.text: A stop-loss guarantees a trade cannot lose more than the planned amount
thinEvidence.note: Stops cap losses in normal conditions, but gaps, slippage and fast markets can fill well beyond the stop.

thinEvidence.text: A .store domain gets more traffic and ranks higher on Google
thinEvidence.note: Search engines state the top-level domain does not affect ranking; the figure is a registry marketing claim.

thinEvidence.text: Students can earn well freelancing or tutoring a skill they already have on flexible hours
thinEvidence.note: Tutoring and freelance work pay real hourly rates, but platform competition is heavy and income stays tied to hours.

thinEvidence.text: A sublet short-term rental only cash-flows if revenue is a multiple of the rent, not merely above it
thinEvidence.note: Cleaning, utilities, platform fees, furniture amortization and vacancy mean revenue near rent is a loss.

thinEvidence.text: Subscription software can flag mispriced lines and reduce advantage betting to minutes a day
thinEvidence.note: Positive-EV tools do flag soft lines quickly, but sportsbooks limit winning accounts fast, so the edge is short-lived.

thinEvidence.text: Success-advice media profits from keeping its audience anxious and unsuccessful
thinEvidence.note: An argument about incentives and intent, not a measurable claim.

thinEvidence.text: Success depends more on a support system, coachability and consistency than on the perfect program
thinEvidence.note: Motivational framing; the components are not operationalized.

thinEvidence.text: A sustained win rate above the sportsbook's implied probability yields profit over many bets despite individual losses
thinEvidence.note: As a conditional statement this is basic expected-value arithmetic; the hard part, which the claim does not deny, is having and keeping such an edge.

thinEvidence.text: It takes about a year of full-time work for dropshipping to replace an average income
thinEvidence.note: Plausible for those who succeed, but there is no independent data and most stores never get there.

thinEvidence.text: Third-party sellers cannot win listings where Amazon itself sells, because Amazon undercuts on price and holds the buy box
thinEvidence.note: Amazon retail has structural cost advantages and the buy-box algorithm favours price, so competing on its own listings is a well-known losing proposition.

thinEvidence.text: Third-party tracking of a signal provider's account makes its performance claims trustworthy
thinEvidence.note: Verified tracking confirms trades on one account but cannot rule out cherry-picked or demo accounts, and past results do not predict future ones.

thinEvidence.text: TikTok's algorithm can push a single video from a tiny account to millions of views
thinEvidence.note: TikTok distributes by interest rather than follower count, so small accounts occasionally go viral, though it is rare.

thinEvidence.text: Timeshares are a financial scheme that leaves buyers worse off and hard to exit
thinEvidence.note: Timeshares depreciate immediately, carry rising maintenance fees and have almost no resale market; consumer regulators treat exit scams as a direct consequence.

thinEvidence.text: AI is a tool, not the business; money comes from solving problems people already pay for
thinEvidence.note: Framing about where value comes from.

thinEvidence.text: Trading apps that filter scam and bundled tokens make meme coin trading safe
thinEvidence.note: Filters catch some rug pulls, but most meme coins still collapse toward zero and most traders of them lose money.

thinEvidence.text: Trading gurus commonly present simulated or demo account results as real trading profits
thinEvidence.note: Regulators require simulated-results disclaimers because the practice is common; prevalence is not measured.

thinEvidence.text: Trading jargon is used to manufacture an illusion of expertise that only the course can teach
thinEvidence.note: A claim about persuasion technique, not a measurable result.

thinEvidence.text: Trading mandates restrict which instruments a trader may trade, not just position size
thinEvidence.note: Standard bank mandate structure; instrument restrictions are part of every desk's limits.

thinEvidence.text: Trading only in the direction of the prevailing trend raises the odds of a winning trade
thinEvidence.note: Trend-following has modest documented returns in currencies over months, but reading the trend off a chart gives little short-term edge after costs.

thinEvidence.text: Trying to capture market returns while avoiding their volatility through trading or leverage usually fails.
thinEvidence.note: Investor return-gap studies show timing and tactical strategies underperform buy-and-hold on average.

thinEvidence.text: A typical side hustle can pay off an average credit-card balance within months
thinEvidence.note: The figure uses mean side-hustle income; at the median it would take years, not months.

thinEvidence.text: UGC creators are paid for the content itself, so they can earn without any following
thinEvidence.note: UGC deals pay for content and usage rights on brand channels, so follower count matters far less than in influencer deals.

thinEvidence.text: Unregulated offshore brokers promoted by gurus can take deposits with no recourse
thinEvidence.note: Regulator warning lists and enforcement actions document offshore forex broker fraud.

thinEvidence.text: Unreliable freelancers who vanish with project assets are a major cost of outsourced content
thinEvidence.note: A common complaint in outsourced creative work; frequency unmeasured.

thinEvidence.text: Unusual options-flow alerts reveal institutional orders that retail day traders can profitably follow
thinEvidence.note: Order flow carries some information in academic data, but public flow alerts arrive late and noisy, and nothing shows retail traders profit from following them.

thinEvidence.text: Using low-down-payment owner-occupant loans to buy many rentals is mortgage fraud that lenders detect
thinEvidence.note: Occupancy misrepresentation on a mortgage application is federal fraud and underwriters check recent loans.

thinEvidence.text: A vending machine route can be started with a used machine for a few hundred dollars and returns depend mostly on location
thinEvidence.note: Used machines are cheap and location drives returns, but a typical machine nets modest sums and restocking is ongoing labor.

thinEvidence.text: Ventures with co-founders and employee equity succeed where solo ventures fail
thinEvidence.note: Startup studies find mixed results: co-founded companies raise more and grow faster, but solo founders have comparable survival in some datasets.

thinEvidence.text: Video reviews with affiliate links convert better than written blog reviews
thinEvidence.note: Video can build trust and reach, but written search content still converts well for purchase-intent queries and there is no clear independent comparison.

thinEvidence.text: The vig on even-money bets takes a sizeable cut of every wager and has been rising
thinEvidence.note: Standard vig is around 4-5% on -110 lines; some markets are juiced higher, but the extreme figure is not typical.

thinEvidence.text: Viral hits from trends cannot be replicated and do not build a returning audience
thinEvidence.note: Trend-driven views churn; retention and returning viewers drive sustained channel revenue.

thinEvidence.text: Viral views do not convert to sales when the audience is the wrong demographic
thinEvidence.note: Views from regions or audiences unlikely to buy do not convert, as ad-targeting data shows.

thinEvidence.text: Visible luxury spending is evidence of money spent, not of wealth held.
thinEvidence.note: Millionaire-household studies show modest consumption; conspicuous spending correlates poorly with net worth.

thinEvidence.text: Visitors judge a store's trustworthiness within seconds, so generic-looking stores lose sales before the copy is read
thinEvidence.note: Web credibility research supports fast first impressions, but the effect size on conversion for dropshipping stores is not independently measured.

thinEvidence.text: Wash trading, where sellers buy from their own wallets to fake demand, is rampant in NFT markets
thinEvidence.note: Blockchain analytics firms found wash trades made up a large share of NFT volume on several marketplaces in 2021-2022.

thinEvidence.text: Wealth is created by making things people want, not redistributed from a fixed pie.
thinEvidence.note: Long-run growth in real output is the standard evidence against zero-sum wealth.

thinEvidence.text: Wealth creation is positive-sum, so everyone can become wealthy
thinEvidence.note: Total wealth grows, but being wealthy is largely relative and scarce assets are constrained, so positive-sum growth does not mean everyone can become wealthy.

thinEvidence.text: Whole life cash value is part of the death benefit, so you cannot collect both
thinEvidence.note: In standard whole life the insurer pays the face amount minus outstanding loans; the cash value is not paid on top.

thinEvidence.text: Whole life insurance cash value can be accessed through policy loans without the taxes and penalties of retirement accounts
thinEvidence.note: Policy loans are generally untaxed and penalty-free, but they accrue interest, early surrender charges apply, and a lapse with loans outstanding can trigger tax.

thinEvidence.text: Wholesale deal flow scales roughly linearly with outbound call volume at a given skill level.
thinEvidence.note: Volume raises deal count, but list quality and diminishing returns on the same leads make it sub-linear.

thinEvidence.text: Wholesale reselling of branded products on Amazon needs no ads because demand already exists on the listing
thinEvidence.note: Demand on existing listings is real, but brand gating and buy-box competition with other resellers squeeze margins on popular items.

thinEvidence.text: Winning dropshipping products are trending, hard to find in stores, and solve a real problem
thinEvidence.note: Reasonable heuristics, but trending products are also the most copied, so the criteria do not secure margin.

thinEvidence.text: Workflow-automation skills can be learned from free videos in a couple of weeks well enough to sell to businesses
thinEvidence.note: No-code tools are quick to learn for simple workflows, but reliable client systems and selling them take longer for most beginners.

thinEvidence.text: Working for free for the first clients is the fastest way to start a service business
thinEvidence.note: Free work can buy testimonials and experience, but it also attracts low-commitment clients and does not reliably convert to paid work.

thinEvidence.text: Writing YouTube scripts with AI for other creators pays a reliable freelance income
thinEvidence.note: Scriptwriting gigs exist, but freelance platforms are crowded, creators increasingly use AI themselves, and income for beginners is irregular rather than reliable.

thinEvidence.text: Years to financial independence depend only on savings rate, not on income level
thinEvidence.note: Mathematically true under constant real returns and equal spending before and after, but low incomes hit a fixed-cost floor that limits achievable savings rates.

thinEvidence.text: Younger adults are more likely than older ones to have a side hustle
thinEvidence.note: Consistent across several independent side-hustle surveys.

thinEvidence.text: YouTube ad revenue can become significant income once a channel is monetized.
thinEvidence.note: Most monetized channels earn little from ads, so significant income is the exception rather than what monetization typically brings.

thinEvidence.text: YouTube ad revenue can reach five figures a month for a channel in a high-paying niche
thinEvidence.note: Finance channels with large audiences do report this; it is the top tail, not the norm.

thinEvidence.text: Credit card limits rise automatically even when the card is barely used
thinEvidence.note: Issuers raise limits based on usage and payment history, and cut dormant lines.

thinEvidence.text: Most of the very wealthy dropped out of college rather than graduating
thinEvidence.note: Surveys of the ultra-wealthy show a large majority hold degrees, many from elite schools.
